business.name: Roofline Canterbury

business.description: Roofline Canterbury is a 100% locally owned and operated roofing and cladding manufacturer and roofing installation contractor. Family owned and Canterbury based since 1977, we manufacture, supply and install long-run roofing and cladding metal from our own Christchurch factory for everything from small home renovations to large commercial developments.
business.emergencyProcess: For urgent leaks or storm damage, call the team on 03 349 8439 during business hours. We prioritise make-safe work and can arrange temporary weather protection while a permanent repair is scheduled.
business.insuranceWork: Yes. We work with homeowners, builders and insurers on re-roofing and repair work across Canterbury, including earthquake and storm-related replacements, and can supply the documentation your insurer needs.

faqs.q: Do you manufacture the roofing yourselves?
faqs.a: Yes. We manufacture long-run roofing, cladding, spouting and flashings in our own Christchurch factory, which is how we keep turnaround times fast and quality consistent.

faqs.q: Can I buy supply-only, or do you install as well?
faqs.a: Both. We manufacture and supply product for your own builder, and we have our own installation team for complete supply and install jobs.

faqs.q: Can you price from my house plans?
faqs.a: Yes, use the Price Your Plans service. Send your plans through the contact form and we measure and price your roofing, cladding and spouting from the drawings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between corrugate and Roofdeck?
faqs.a: Corrugate is the classic round-profile iron, through-fixed with screws, and works from about 8 degrees pitch. Roofdeck is a trapezoidal long-run profile with stronger spanning and a flatter look, working from lower pitches. Both come in ColorCote finishes.
The ColorCote and Zincalume colour ranges cover the popular New Zealand roof colours. Visit the colour options page or ask us for a specific colour match.
Yes. If your existing roof is deprecated asbestos cement sheet, we manage safe removal as part of the re-roofing process and replace it with new long-run steel.

faqs.q: How long does a re-roof take?
faqs.a: Most residential re-roofs are completed in a few working days once product is manufactured and on site. Because we manufacture locally, lead times are typically shorter than importing.
We cover greater Christchurch and Canterbury, including Selwyn, Waimakariri, Ashburton and further afield for larger projects.
